          1 Narita International Airport


                From the web: This mammoth international airport serving the Tokyo area offers direct rail access to the city.

                              53 min · 44.8 mi
                              to Tokyo Station


                   Take the JR Narita Express (N'EX) — direct, no transfers, ~53 minutes.
                   Fare: ¥3,070/person (~¥18,400 for 6)
                   Reserve seats together in advance so the group sits as one.
                   Luggage racks on board — no need to haul bags between platforms.
                   Cheaper alternative (if budget matters more than convenience): Keisei Skyliner to Nippori (~36–41 min, ¥2,580) + 1 stop on JR Yamanote
                   Line to Tokyo Station (~20 min, ~¥200). Total ~¥2,780/person, one transfer required.

                From the web: 400-year-old iconic market studded with stalls offering all manner of Japanese edibles.

                              to Daigo-ji

                     • Walk from Daigo Station to Daigo-ji (~10–15 min).
                     • Total: ~50–55 min · ~¥260–300/person

          3 Hozugawa River Boat Ride End Point


                reach by 11am
                From the web: 2-hr. riverboat ride steered with oars & bamboo poles past rapids, deep-water pools & lush scenery.

                              to Arashiyama Yoshimura


                   Hozugawa River Cruise End Point → Arashiyama Bridge (Togetsukyo Bridge)
                     • Get off at the Hozugawa River Boat Ride End Point.
                     • Walk downstream toward Togetsukyo Bridge (~5–10 min).
                     • The landing point is only a few hundred metres upstream of the bridge.
                     • Total: ~5–10 min · ¥0
                     •
                    So you can essentially walk straight from the cruise endpoint to Togetsukyo Bridge and continue your Arashiyama sightseeing from
                   there.



          4 Arashiyama Yoshimura


                need book
                From the web: Hand-cut soba noodles made with domestically sourced buckwheat in a leafy riverside locale.


                              2 min · 400 ft


          5 Togetsukyō Bridge


                Open 24 hours • Spring blossoms, fall colors & mountains can be viewed from this famed wood bridge.

                              6 min · 2 mi
                              to Otagi Nenbutsuji Temple


                   Arashiyama → Otagi Nenbutsuji Temple
                      • From Togetsukyo Bridge, walk north through Arashiyama toward Saga-Toriimoto.
                      • Continue along the historic Saga-Toriimoto preserved street to Otagi Nenbutsuji.
                      • Walking: ~35–45 min · ¥0
                   1. Bamboo Grove / Saga area
                   If you haven't already visited the main Bamboo Grove, you can pass through the northern end as you head toward Otagi.
                   2. Tenryu-ji area
                   You'll pass near Tenryu-ji. The gardens are beautiful, but I'd only enter if you have extra time.
                   3. Adashino Nenbutsuji              ⭐
                   This is probably the best stop along the route. It has thousands of small stone Buddhist statues spread across a hillside and is much
                   quieter than central Arashiyama.
                   4. Saga-Toriimoto Preserved Street                    ⭐
                   One of the nicest parts of the walk. Traditional wooden townhouses line the road, giving you a much more old-fashioned Kyoto
                   atmosphere.
                   5. Otagi Nenbutsuji           ⭐⭐⭐
                      • Your destination and arguably the highlight. It's famous for its 1,200+ expressive stone Rakan statues, each with a different
                        expression.
                      • when walking




          6 Otagi Nenbutsuji Temple


                got secret bamboo forest path 1hour
                From the web: Buddhist temple founded in the 8th century, featuring more than 1,200 stone heads on its grounds.

          5 Amaharashi Coast (Noto Peninsula Quasi-National Park)


                1. See Onnaiwa Rock + Tateyama Mountains                      ⭐⭐⭐
                  • The signature view of Amaharashi.
                  • On a clear day, you can see the 3,000 m-high Tateyama Mountain Range rising behind Toyama Bay.
                  • Particularly beautiful in winter when the mountains are snow-covered.
                  •
                2. Walk along Amaharashi Beach                      ⭐⭐⭐
                  • Walk along the sandy coastline and pine trees.
                  • Take photos of the sea, Onnaiwa and mountains.
                  • The coast is free to visit and open year-round.
                  •
                3. Visit Roadside Station Amaharashi                     ⭐⭐
                  • Only about 5 minutes from Amaharashi Station.
                  • Has an observation deck, café, local food and Takaoka crafts.
                  • Great place to warm up if you're visiting in December.
                  •
                4. See Yoshitsune Rock
                  • A small historical spot associated with the legend of Minamoto no Yoshitsune taking shelter from the rain here.
                  • It's one of the area's cultural points of interest.
                  •
                5. Photograph the Himi Line                  🚃📸
                  • One of the coolest photo opportunities is the JR Himi Line running right beside the coastline.
                  • You can get shots of the train with the ocean and mountains behind it.

                              to Takaoka

                   HOTEL NEW NAGANO NEXT

                From the web: Karuizawa is a resort town in the mountains near Nagano, Japan. It's known for mild summers conducive to outdoor
                recreation like golf. Forests in the surrounding area offer cycling and walking paths along with sites like Kumoba Pond and Shiraito Falls.
                Skiing and hot springs are popular in the winter. Kyu-Karuizawa, the old town center, is the site of a pedestrian shopping strip.
